newsitem.title: UK: LME base metals calm in late trade.
newsitem.headline: LME base metals calm in late trade.

text.p: Base metals prices were little changed in late trading on Tuesday, apart from slightly firmer copper, after a speculative sell-off swept the complex lower earlier in the day.
Three months copper ticked up to as high as $2,160/65 per tonne by 1800 GMT, compared to $2,145 at the kerb close and $2,162 at Monday's finish.
Prices had dropped to a low of $2,118 -- the lowest level since December 1996 -- at one point in the fund-led selling spree during London Metal Exchange (LME) trading.
But key support held at $2,120 and copper managed to stage a bounce.
In other metals, aluminium was virtually unchanged at $1,634/38 compared to $1,634 at the kerb close, which was down $43 on the day.
Zinc, also wounded in the sell-off, was holding steady at $1,477/$82.
